items.followUp: Differentiate between moment of force and centre of gravity.

rubric.why: Identifies torque as the turning effect of a force about an axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining forces of a couple.
rubric.description: Describes the forces in a couple.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a couple consists of equal, opposite, parallel forces.

rubric.why: Defines centre of mass in terms of the distribution of mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the point at which the mass of a body may be considered concentrated, or an equivalent definition.

rubric.why: Defines centre of gravity by reference to the body's weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the point through which the body's weight acts.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis.
A couple consists of two equal, opposite and parallel forces acting at different points; it produces rotation.
The centre of mass is the point at which the mass of a body may be considered concentrated.
The centre of gravity is the point through which the weight of a body acts.

items.followUp: Convert 68°F into degrees Celsius and kelvin.

rubric.why: Uses the correct Fahrenheit-to-Celsius relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula C = 5/9(F − 32), or an equivalent form.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given temperature and obtains the Celsius value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and/or obtaining 37°C.

rubric.why: Uses the Celsius-to-kelvin relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for K = C + 273 (or +273.15).

rubric.why: Gives the converted temperature on the kelvin scale.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 310 K (or 310.15 K); award 1 mark if the method is correct but there is a minor arithmetic error.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 98.6°F
Formula: C = 5/9(F − 32)
Formula: K = C + 273

items.followUp: Define least count and state the least count of a measuring tape marked in millimetres.

rubric.why: States that least count is the smallest measurement an instrument can measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an equivalent definition of least count.

rubric.why: Gives the standard least count of a metre rod.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1 mm or 0.1 cm.

modelAnswer: Least count is the smallest measurement that can be measured by an instrument.
The least count of a metre rod is 1 mm (0.1 cm).

items.followUp: Express 4500000 W in kilowatts and megawatts using prefixes.

rubric.why: Correctly expresses the watt value in kilowatts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 3200 kW.

rubric.why: Correctly expresses the watt value in megawatts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 3.2 MW.

items.followUp: Explain what happens to a moving car when its brakes are applied and when its tyres lose grip on the road.

rubric.why: Explains braking as reducing or stopping motion by applying brakes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that braking reduces or stops a vehicle's motion by applying brakes.

rubric.why: Explains skidding as the tyres sliding or slipping on the road.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an equivalent description of skidding.

modelAnswer: Braking is the action of applying brakes to reduce or stop the motion of a vehicle.
Skidding is the sliding or slipping of a vehicle's tyres on the road instead of rolling normally.

items.followUp: State the relation between force and the rate of change of momentum.

rubric.why: States Newton's second-law relation between force and momentum change.
rubric.description: Relates force to change in momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that force is the rate of change of momentum, or writing F = Δp/Δt.

rubric.why: Gives the equivalent fixed-mass form or the direction of the change.
rubric.description: Gives the implication of the relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = ma for constant mass, or stating that the momentum changes in the direction of the force.

modelAnswer: Force is equal to the rate of change of momentum: F = Δp/Δt.
For a body of constant mass, this becomes F = ma; the momentum changes in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Define resultant force and state how it is found for several forces.

rubric.why: Defines the resultant as one force equivalent to the combined action of the forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a single force with the same effect as all the forces acting together.

rubric.why: States that the resultant is found by vector addition.
rubric.description: States how to find the resultant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant is the vector sum of the forces.

modelAnswer: A resultant force is a single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting together.
It is found by taking the vector sum of the forces.

items.followUp: Define translatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Defines rotatory motion as motion around an axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body rotates about an axis.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of a rotating body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example such as a fan, wheel or Earth rotating about its axis.

modelAnswer: Rotatory motion is the motion of a body around an axis.
The blades of a rotating fan are an example of rotatory motion.
